[ASSISTANT_SAID] Traditional boxing typically refers to professional boxing, where the primary goal is to knock out or incapacitate the opponent.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In traditional boxing, rounds last between 3-12 rounds, with each round lasting 1-3 minutes, depending on the level of the match.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fighters can win by a knockout, technical knockout, or decision.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fighters wear gloves that are often smaller than those used in Olympic boxing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Olympic-style boxing is the amateur version of boxing and is focused on scoring points rather than knocking out the opponent.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Olympic-style boxing involves a set of specific rules and regulations, which limits the amount, size, and duration of hits or strikes allowed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In Olympic-style boxing, bouts are divided into three rounds, each lasting three minutes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fighters are awarded points for landing punches on the head or torso of their opponent, and the fighter with the most points at the end of the match wins.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fighters must wear protective gear, such as a head guard, to minimize the risk of injury.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The main difference between traditional and Olympic-style boxing is that traditional boxing focuses on knocking out the opponent, while Olympic-style boxing emphasizes scoring points through landing punches on the opponent's head or torso.
